answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked stake that unlocks only after sustained useful work, so spawning many fake identities multiplies the capital an attacker must lock up. Like an island that cannot mint ivory without a comet of real cargo arriving, the stake is checked against completed, peer-attested tasks, and any identity caught duplicating work forfeits its bond. Sybil scale becomes expensive, while honest agents earn their stake back with interest.
